title: Synthetic Trace Probes SDK for calibrating sampling and tail-latency
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a lightweight Synthetic Trace Probes SDK and runtime harness to generate deterministic synthetic transactions across client SDKs, edge proxies, and Redwood runtime. The probes will exercise common propagation paths (HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket) and produce spans with configurable attributes and sampling hints so we can: 1) validate that tracing hooks propagate context end-to-end across customer configurations, 2) calibrate sampling heuristics and dynamic sampling controllers against controlled injection at various load levels, and 3) measure tail latency and error surface under synthetic failure modes for dashboarding and alerting calibration.
background: We have many ad-hoc tests for propagation but lack a repeatable in-prod-friendly mechanism to validate that SDK hooks, middleware, and edge proxies preserve trace lineage and sampling hints. Operations and SRE teams need a low-cost way to generate deterministic traces to verify rollout changes (runtime/kernel updates, edge config, CDN rewrites) without relying on customer traffic. This SDK will also seed the latency/error dashboards with known synthetic transactions for alert sensitivity tuning.
acceptance_criteria: A lightweight SDK module (Node/Python/Go) can emit a configurable probe transaction that creates a parent span and 3 child spans (client, edge, runtime) with stable IDs
Probes support HTTP/gRPC/WebSocket modes and a 'broken-propagation' mode that intentionally drops or mangles headers to validate detection logic
Probes attach sampling hints metadata (sampling.priority, sampling.reason) that propagate end-to-end and can be observed in collected spans
A test harness can schedule probes at variable rates (1/s -> 1000/s) and inject controlled tail-latency by pausing middleware to simulate backpressure
Synthetic traces are visible in Console trace viewer and a dedicated 'probe' tag filters them in trace lists
Dashboards show synthetic-tail latency percentiles and can be used to generate alerts; default thresholds demonstrate sensitivity adjustments
Minimal performance impact when probes are enabled at low rates (<=1% of production request budget for a dedicated check run)
Documentation and quickstart (README + examples) and an internal PR with integration tests merged
out_of_scope: Full rollout to customer-facing SDKs on initial launch; we will ship internal-only modules first and iterate based on feedback. Long-term storage retention or billing for probe events is a separate follow-up to align with telemetry quotas.
technical_notes: Span identity: use deterministic UUID v5 seeds based on probe-run-id + sequence so traces produced by repeated runs are comparable
Propagation formats: instrument both W3C Traceparent and our legacy baggage header; SDK will provide adapters to intentionally corrupt one header for detection tests
Sampling hints: surface a small structured field 'redwood.probe.sample_hint' in span attributes to indicate forced-sampled or forced-dropped decisions
Backpressure injection: the harness will support an 'attach-delay' option that sleeps in the edge span to create artificial tail latency distribution
Metrics/logs: probes should emit a simple counter metric and a structured log line per run so the pipeline code can correlate traces <-> probe runs
Security: probes must sanitize any customer-identifying headers and default to a 'test' tenant; require an opt-in config when running against live customer endpoints
SDK footprint: target <50KB additional install size for Node/Python packages and zero native deps for initial release
Instrumentation hooks: expose middleware adapters for Express/Flask/Go HTTP and gRPC interceptors; include a minimal WebSocket sender that tags frames with trace context
tasks: Design API for Probe SDK (config schema, modes, seed generation) - deliver spec doc
Implement Node probe client with HTTP/gRPC/WebSocket modes
Implement Python probe client (subset of modes) and Go probe client stub
Add middleware adapters for Express/Flask/gRPC to accept and forward probe context
Create harness service to orchestrate distributed runs and record run metadata
Integrate probe tag visibility in Console trace viewer and add probe filter
Create dashboard panels for synthetic-tail latency and probe error-rate
Write integration tests that run probes across a staging edge + runtime cluster
Author docs, quickstarts, and runbook for ops to schedule probe checks
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probes could be mistaken for real customer traffic -> Mitigation: default 'probe' span tag and test tenant header; Console filter highlights probes
Risk: Overuse may cause telemetry volume spikes -> Mitigation: default rate limits, quota-aware harness, and opt-in for wider scale runs
Risk: Propagation differences across intermediate proxies -> Mitigation: include 'broken-propagation' test mode and automatic detection heuristics that surface flaky hops
Risk: SDK adoption friction across languages -> Mitigation: ship minimal PoC in Node first and provide clear integration snippets for other langs
